title: Berberine: A Natural Compound with Broad-Spectrum Pharmacological Effects and Translational Potential
venue: International Journal of Newgen Research in Pharmacy & Healthcare
abstract: Berberine is a naturally derived isoquinoline alkaloid with extensive pharmacological activities encompassing antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, cardioprotective, neuroprotective, hepatoprotective, anticancer, and antimicrobial effects. Its broad-spectrum bioactivity is mediated mainly through modulation of critical signaling pathways including AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), which coordinate cellular energy homeostasis, inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and autophagy. The compound’s ability to regulate metabolic functions, inhibit tumor progression, protect cardiovascular and nervous systems, modulate gut microbiota, and combat resistant pathogens validates its therapeutic versatility. Despite significant progress in elucidation of its molecular mechanisms and experimental efficacy, clinical translation is constrained by poor oral bioavailability, dose optimization challenges, safety concerns, and a lack of large-scale rigorous clinical trials. Innovations in nanoformulations, structural optimization, and more robust clinical studies are pivotal future directions to overcome these limitations and maximize berberine’s therapeutic potential.
